dedupe_keys.name: bitre heavy vehicle median speed on capital city routes australia

description: Australia's Bureau of Infrastructure and Transport Research Economics (BITRE) uses freight vehicle telematics to measure traffic congestion for heavy vehicles on selected routes in the five mainland state capitals, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth. The selected routes are the major motorways, highways and arterial roads used by both passenger and freight vehicles, 71 routes in the 2022 release, the fourth in an annual series started in 2019. The layers give the median speed of a sample of heavy vehicles on each OpenStreetMap road segment (motorway, trunk and primary classes and their links) by hour of the day, day of the week and month of the year, for 2021 and 2022. Coverage is the five capital cities. The data are free under Creative Commons Attribution, published as ArcGIS feature services in the Digital Atlas of Australia with copies on data.gov.au, and the processing method is in BITRE's GitHub repository and the National Freight Data Hub catalogue; road segments are OpenStreetMap data under the Open Database Licence. Caveats: speeds come from a sample of telematics-equipped heavy vehicles, only main road classes are covered, and each year uses a January OpenStreetMap snapshot. The speeds support calibration of freight network flow and capacity planning models and baselines for disruption studies. It complements the Australian national roads dataset.
